summary: Sustained 5xx elevation during steady small-payload QPS with keepalive fragmentation and upstream restart cycles
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-12 ~11:05 UTC NovaPay reported elevated 5xx errors for their dedicated cluster during steady ~1.5k rps of small JSON payloads (~200B). Errors surfaced as 502/503/504 from the API Gateway with a correlated increase in upstream runtime restarts. Impact: Customer-facing API error rate rose from baseline <0.1% to 6-12% for ~45 minutes causing client failures in payment verification flows. Environment: prod/us-east (dedicated pool customer NovaPay, tenant-id nvyp-034). Observed behavior: High 5xx rate, streaming session resets, intermittent EPIPE/EINVAL on runtime-side HTTP/2 writes, API Gateway logs show 'upstream reset' and 'half-closed stream' messages. Metrics show keepalive connection pool fragmentation: large fraction of live sockets with TTL <60s and frequent short-lived worker processes. Autoscaler activity: small-scale oscillation (scale-down followed by immediate scale-up) at ~11:04-11:07. Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay customer's small-payload steady QPS against dedicated endpoint (test harness attached). 2) Start with ~1.5k rps with 100 concurrent keepalives. 3) Observe accept/keepalive pool churn and increased 5xx. Logs/metrics: API Gateway p95 latency unchanged; p50 normal; error rate spike correlates with worker PID churn and kernel cgroup CPU throttling events on nodes. nvml and dmesg show intermittent 'CPU quota exceeded' throttles aligning to scale-down windows. Hypothesis: scale-down triggers cgroup reassign that briefly starves runtimes or causes runtime child processes to exit/restart; combined with keepalive fragmentation (short-lived sockets) and HTTP/2 stream half-close leads to proxy returning 502/503 instead of graceful retry. Attachments: customer request logs, replay script, grafana snapshots. Next steps: SRE to prevent scale-down during customer sustain, patch runtime to tolerate partial write EPIPE, add guard in API gateway to backoff instead of immediate 502, run controlled replay and validate fix.

11:22 UTC - SRE (Diego) captured runtime core dump sequence: child processes performing short-lived exits with SIGCHLD observed; runtime logs show 'failed to flush http2 frame: EPIPE' before restart
11:30 UTC - Observed kernel CPU throttling events (cgroup quota) across 3/6 nodes in the dedicated pool; timestamps align to AZ-level scale-down scripts
11:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation applied: paused autoscaler scale-down for NovaPay pool, error rate dropped back to ~0.5% within 6 minutes
12:05 UTC - Engineering note: probable race between scale-down cgroup reassign + HTTP/2 stream management producing proxy upstream resets
12:30 UTC - Reproducer run (1.5k rps small payload) against canary with scale-down disabled confirms reduced 5xx; with scale-down enabled reproduces 5xx spike

Priya Nair (Eng) 2026-03-12 13:05 UTC: Drafted PR to change API Gateway behavior to triangulate upstream resets and apply soft-retry rather than immediate 502 when request body appears complete; seeking review.
resolution: Mitigation: paused autoscaler scale-down for affected dedicated pool (NovaPay) which reduced 5xx to baseline. Long-term: engineering has prioritized two actions: 1) runtime patch to avoid fast-exit on partial HTTP/2 write failures (EPIPE/EINVAL) and to attempt graceful drain/reconnect, target patch in runtime v1.12.4; 2) api-gateway change to soft-retry on transient upstream stream resets. Follow-ups: formal postmortem scheduled, autoscaler scale-down heuristics to be updated to avoid concurrent cgroup reassign during high keepalive utilization windows.
